methods.name: Glaze
methods.evidence: The official FAQ distinguishes style protection from inconsistent img2img protection. Do not treat it as an editing or video shield.

methods.name: Nightshade
methods.evidence: Aims to affect models trained on poisoned examples. It is not immediate protection against an already-trained editor.

methods.name: PhotoGuard
methods.evidence: Encoder and end-to-end diffusion perturbations. White-box results are not guarantees for other models or transformations.

methods.name: Mist / Mist v2
methods.evidence: Adversarial image preprocessing. Upstream calls it watermarking and has licensing-language ambiguity; excluded from built-in defaults under the no-watermark requirement.

methods.name: DiffusionGuard
methods.evidence: Early-diffusion objective with mask augmentation. RIPOSTE now has optional early 9-channel inpainting conditioning and masked optimization, not a reproduction or a validated pretrained defense.

methods.name: DCT-Shield
methods.evidence: Optimizes DCT coefficients. RIPOSTE uses real JPEG-forward views, approximate backward gradients and frequency-weighted updates, not DCT-Shield or a strict frequency-domain constraint.

methods.name: I2VGuard
methods.evidence: Spatial, temporal and diffusion attack modules; CVPR 2025. Temporal objectives must be evaluated on generated video.

methods.name: Vid-Freeze
methods.evidence: Attention suppression targets static or near-static generated videos. Motion failure and loss of source-content recognition are distinct outcomes.

methods.name: Anti-Prompt
methods.evidence: Targets text-conditioned interactions during denoising. The arXiv record reports ECCV 2026 acceptance. Broader transfer remains a test question.

methods.name: I2VShield
methods.evidence: Text-adaptive perturbation generation and multimodal-attention disruption. Deployment/code readiness not established by this release.

methods.name: IPV-Bench / IP-Bench
methods.evidence: v3, August 19 2026: five methods across four I2V models, weak transfer and preprocessing robustness. RIPOSTE adds exact-magnitude sign controls; this does not reproduce the benchmark.

methods.name: Robust-style-mimicry evaluation
methods.evidence: Independent research finds existing perturbation defenses can fail against adaptive attackers. Do not generalize this to a proof that no future defense can improve.
